```artifact
Feature: Doorstop Requirements Management

  As a software system, Doorstop should securely store requirements, manage changes, associate them with developer identifications, be scalable, and provide a lightweight installation method.

  Scenario Outline: Storing and managing requirements

    Given Doorstop is installed
    When requirements are stored
    Then they should be securely stored
    And changes should be managed
    And developer identifications should be associated
    And Doorstop should be scalable
    And installation should be lightweight

    Examples:
      | Requirement ID | Security Level | Change Management | Developer ID | Scalability | Installation Method |
      | RE011          | High           | Yes              | Yes          | High        | Lightweight          |
      | RE012          | High           | Yes              | Yes          | High        | Lightweight          |
      | RE013          | High           | Yes              | Yes          | High        | Lightweight          |
      | RE014          | High           | Yes              | Yes          | High        | Lightweight          |
      | RE015          | High           | Yes              | Yes          | High        | Lightweight          |

  Scenario Outline: Handling requirement changes

    Given Doorstop is installed
    When a requirement change occurs
    Then it should be handled properly
    And it should be associated with a developer
    And Doorstop should remain scalable

    Examples:
      | Requirement ID | Change Management | Developer ID | Scalability |
      | RE011          | Yes              | Yes          | High        |
      | RE012          | Yes              | Yes          | High        |
      | RE013          | Yes              | Yes          | High        |
      | RE014          | Yes              | Yes          | High        |
      | RE015          | Yes              | Yes          | High        |

  Scenario Outline: Associating requirement changes with developer identifications

    Given Doorstop is installed
    When a requirement change occurs
    Then it should be associated with a developer
    And Doorstop should remain scalable

    Examples:
      | Requirement ID | Developer ID | Scalability |
      | RE011          | Yes          | High        |
      | RE012          | Yes          | High        |
      | RE013          | Yes          | High        |
      | RE014          | Yes          | High        |
      | RE015          | Yes          | High        |

  Scenario Outline: Doorstop scalability

    Given Doorstop is installed
    When requirements are added
    Then Doorstop should handle them
    And Doorstop should remain scalable

    Examples:
      | Requirement ID | Scalability |
      | RE011          | High        |
      | RE012          | High        |
      | RE013          | High        |
      | RE014          | High        |
      | RE015          | High        |

  Scenario Outline: Lightweight installation

    Given Doorstop is installed
    When installation is performed
    Then it should be lightweight
    And Doorstop should remain scalable

    Examples:
      | Requirement ID | Installation Method | Scalability |
      | RE011          | Lightweight          | High        |
      | RE012          | Lightweight          | High        |
      | RE013          | Lightweight          | High        |
      | RE014          | Lightweight          | High        |
      | RE015          | Lightweight          | High        |
```
